newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iran oil chief could start border talks in Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Iran oil chief could start border talks in Kuwait.

text.p: Iran's oil minister on Saturday starts an official visit to Kuwait during which the two sides could start border talks on oil-rich northern Gulf waters.

"We expect, especially during the visit of His Excellency the Oil Minister (Gholamreza Aghazadeh) the first negotiations between the two sides in this field" to start, Iran's ambassador to Kuwait, GholamAli Sanati, told Reuters.

"The sea borders are not clear at all...There is oil under all these waters...Riches from God," he said through an Arabic translator of the narrow waterway where economic exclusion zones and other sea borders could overlap.
The visiting minister is not expected to get involved in technical border negotiations which are assigned to the legal departments of the foreign ministries of Kuwait and Iran.
But the two oil ministries are very interested in the issue because they are in charge of oil explorations. Both sides have oil drilling rigs operating in the northern Gulf, Sanati added.

Non-Arab Iran has a coastline along the entire Gulf waterway which its shares with Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and the Arab island state of Bahrain. Iraq, at the northwestern tip of the Gulf, also has access.

"Kuwait would like to first finish talks with the Saudi side then negotiate with Iran to identify the continental drift. Once the continental drift between Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iran is identified we can start discussing with Kuwait," Sanati said.

"I believe they have reached results in their talks with Saudi Arabia and I think a company has been picked for land and sea demarcations...From the side of the Islamic Republic we are fully willing to discuss this."

Aghazadeh, on his first visit to fellow OPEC member Kuwait since shortly after the 1991 Gulf War, is due to deliver a message during his two-day visit to Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah from Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.

Aghazadeh, invited by his Kuwaiti counterpart Isa al-Mazeedi who was appointed in October, is also due to hold talks with the crown prince and prime minister, the foreign minister and parliament speaker.
Sanati said the Iranian side "is ready to cooperate with Kuwait in the oil field, petroleum industries, petrochemicals and joint bilateral or tripartite investment".
Kuwait exports refined oil products worth some $200 million a year to Iran while Iranian exports to Kuwait are worth about $85 million.
